brief.headline: They lost ₹-23.68 Cr last year and sit in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.68) — lead with payment speed (not a price squeeze) and line up Huhtamaki or UFLEX as a second source now.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match Shrinath Roto Pack's ₹290.00/KG on our top three laminates (currently ₹295.00/KG).
priceAsk.target: ₹290.00/KG for LM ELECTRAL sachets — a ₹3.91 L annual saving.
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹290.00/KG to Shrinath Roto Pack for identical laminate SKUs. The market ask for pharma ORS sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg (typical ₹250/kg), and we're paying at the top of that band — so matching our best price is fair.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (half our current 30 days) in exchange for the ₹5/kg price cut — early cash is worth about 10.96% to them.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹9.49 L of our cash, but the ₹3.91 L annual saving more than covers that.

brief.financialLeverage: GLS is fragile: they lost ₹-23.68 Cr in FY2024-25, keep -3.4% profit (peers keep 2.5%), and their Altman Z score is 1.68 (grey zone — halfway to distress). They owe 2.15x their own cash and borrow at about 10.96%. Our ₹2.31 Cr is only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we're tiny to them — but they need every customer's cash right now. Don't push a hard price cut that could tip them over; instead, trade faster payment (which is worth their 10.96% borrowing rate) for the ₹5/kg discount, and quietly start qualifying Huhtamaki or UFLEX so we're not caught if GLS stumbles.

evidence.point: They keep less profit than similar firms.
Their Altman Z score puts them in the grey distress zone.
They borrow at about this rate, so paying early is worth that much to them.
We already pay this much less to Shrinath Roto Pack for the same laminate SKUs.
They owe a lot relative to their own cash.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier — proven and scalable for laminate sachets; a strong second source to qualify now.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant that makes both film and converts it — can handle our laminate volume at scale; second-source to qualify now.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global group's India converter for pharma blister and sachet laminates (health D 31/100, revenue ₹222.04 Cr) — a credible backup, though weaker health than the listed options.

risks: They have severe legal cases, GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and high debt — all red flags that supply could stumble.
Their overall money-health score is 2/10 and credit rating is IVR BBB- / Stable — middling at best; don't put too much volume through them without a backup.
Pushing a hard price cut could push a loss-making, grey-zone supplier over the edge — we risk losing supply if we squeeze too hard on headline price.
We're only 0.33% of their revenue, so we have almost no leverage on price alone — the win is in trading faster payment (which they badly need) for the discount.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and we'd like to secure more volume with you — but we need you at ₹290/kg to match what we pay Shrinath, and in return we can pay you in 15 days instead of 30 to help your cash flow.
